The game itself is definetly nice but there are some issues outside the gameplay.

First, you can't go full screen if your screen's refresh rate is NOT 60Hz.
Second, there is a lag between mouse clicking because of double-clicking.
Third, the disable double-clicking option is NOT working
Fourth, the default key mapping for K/M is terrible and you can't bind mouse side buttons.

You should play this game with a controller, or a mouse with side buttons that can map keyboard keys.

Positive:
- Well optimized.
- Great art (music, equipment design, environment).
- Most enemies stop respawning after killing them ~12 times.

Negative:
- Running back to bosses everytime you die. It is not much of a problem if you upgrade your weapons, you will kill most of them in 1-5 tries. But still, terrible design decision.
- Too much ganking which gives a huge advantage to longer weapons. Small ones are way worse.
- Takes too long to find weapons, which detracts from replayability. You are going to play a good chunk of the game with the same weapons until you find the one you actually want to use.
- You can upgrade your weapons by using limited resources, but now you are in a way "forced" to only use the weapons you upgraded.
- Gameplay is badly explained, requires reading wikis (e.g. I-frames can be improved by leveling certain attributes).
- Almost all consumables are finite. They give you enough but still, why? No reason to. They end up limiting gameplay, since you dont know how hard the next boss is going to be, so you will accumulate a bunch. It would be way better if you had infinite uses or if you could recharge on bonfires.
- Many boring bosses that also look lame.

Before I played DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin, I had no friends, no girlfriend, and no will to live.
After finishing it… yeah, same.
But at least now I can dodge roll through existential dread and say “Git Gud” to my therapist.
It’s Dark Souls. You suffer, you rage, you win. Worth it.

Then there’s the hitboxes — forged by demons, blessed by RNG, and designed to personally offend you.
Every boss feels like a toxic relationship you keep going back to because “maybe this time will be different.”
Spoiler: it’s not.

But when that victory screen finally pops up after your 57th attempt, you ascend to another plane of existence.
Suddenly, your problems don’t matter anymore — because you are now the problem.
Praise the sun, curse the fog gate, and never trust a chest again.

DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin is a fun, challenging and rewarding installment in the Dark Souls series! With improvements to graphics, framerates, and connectivity, coupled with better character build diversity and tighter hit-boxes; it arguably stands as one of FROMSoft's stronger titles...

...but if all the above is true, then why is it critisized so heavily by some? Because it's a "meat-grinder" of a game. The game has no mercy upon sinner or saint and chastizes imminent failures by progressively nerfing the player, highlighting all inherent weaknesses the player attempts to hide with armor or estus. Your "hero" status is earned second by bloody second and a spine is grown only through raw experience.
It's brilliant! ...or, it's evil? Either way, this mechanic coupled with an oppressive AI, bosses that will 1-shot obliterate you and friendly NPCs that mock the futility of your personal struggle... it's no mystery why casual-gamers (pansies) don't oft return.

If you have familiarity with Dark Souls titles and are willing to invest some effort and stomach failure to "git gud", then Scholar of the First Sin is an experience I couldn't speak more highly of. By the end of your journey, you'll stand a little taller, smile a little wider and quetly rejoice knowing your Dark Souls "nuts" are dragging on the ground behind you.

...UMBASA!

On this volume, they introduced the TP system of each bonfire discovered, which helps immensely in moving between distant points, and also the torches can be used to illuminate dark places.

Like in Dark Souls 1, the online mode is still disabled. If you are thinking about giving this game a chance, remember that this game was designed to die A LOT of times, so take it easy.

As far as souls games feel, Ds2 carries a completely different feel compared to the other games. The freedom of the game was fantastic. It reminded me of how Elden ring allowed players to explore other areas if they were stuck on a particular boss. The design of the levels felt the most souls-like out of the games. You’d get punished for running through an area and the game forces you to slow down consistently. Some of the content and npc questlines can be ridiculously ambiguous and unforgiving, even more so than the other souls games. But much of the grind is worth it. Mechanically the game has its own feel and movement to learn. It can feel outdated and sluggish, but you can’t fault the game considering how old it’s getting. Some of the stats to level like adaptability should be articulated better (especially since it affects invincibility windows). This game gets unnecessary hate but by no means is it perfect. At times it will seem poorly designed but that’s part of the whole experience.

I imagine the original Dark Souls as the first born of Miyazaki and Dark Souls 2 as the middle child. Miyazaki poured a ton of love and effort into making Dark Souls a thoroughly connected and well designed world, but when Dark Souls 2 happened the novelty of kids wore off and he lost interest. So the middle child did his best to imitate the elder son, but he emphasized the wrong things (difficulty) over the right things (level design, enemy designs) and Miyazaki was too busy with the newborn (Bloodborne) to give a sh*t. So when Dark Souls 2 grew enough to be released it was alright but compared to the rest of the family is just a disappointment, and everytime you go to his house you say "hey where's your brother Dark Souls?" and the poor kid feels insecure and inadequate. And then he kills himself and you shrug and go replay Dark Souls.

It's not bad though.
